newNodes.name: Food-sharing norms
newNodes.emerged: ~100 kya and earlier: shared butchery at hearths; demand-sharing universal among recorded foragers
newNodes.prereqRationale: fire_making: the kill is cooked and divided at the common hearth; the sharing rule grows around it.
newNodes.rationale: fire_making: the kill is cooked and divided at the common hearth; the sharing rule grows around it.
newNodes.desc: Whoever brings in meat must share it with the whole band. A hunter's bad week no longer starves his children, and no family hoards while others go hungry.
newNodes.effectRationale: Sharing pools the band's food, so children of unlucky hunters are fed in lean seasons.
newNodes.distinctFrom: gift_exchange moves goods between bands; food sharing divides food within the band.

newNodes.name: Seasonal round
newNodes.emerged: ~23 kya Ohalo II (Sea of Galilee): brush huts reoccupied season after season
newNodes.prereqRationale: shelter_hut: a scheduled round returns to known base camps with built shelters.
newNodes.rationale: shelter_hut: a scheduled round returns to known base camps with built shelters.
newNodes.desc: The band moves between known camps on a fixed yearly schedule, reaching fish runs, nut groves and herds when each is at its best.
newNodes.effectRationale: A scheduled round exploits a wider territory than a single camp, so the settlement draws on a larger hinterland.
newNodes.distinctFrom: transhumance (A2) moves herds between pastures; the seasonal round moves the whole band between wild resources.

newNodes.name: Fire-stick land management
newNodes.emerged: ~45 kya change in Sahul fire regimes (contested); recorded Aboriginal mosaic burning
newNodes.prereqRationale: fire_making: deliberate burning is a use of controlled fire.
newNodes.rationale: fire_making: deliberate burning is a use of controlled fire.
newNodes.desc: The band burns country in small patches at chosen seasons, opening grassland that draws game and renews food plants.
newNodes.effectRationale: Fresh regrowth and concentrated game shorten the lean season, so fewer die of hunger in bad years.
newNodes.distinctFrom: fire_making is the technique; this is the shared rule of when and where the band burns its land.

newNodes.name: Communal storehouses
newNodes.emerged: ~9,300 BCE Dhra' (Jordan): free-standing granaries shared by the settlement
newNodes.prereqRationale: cereal_cultivation: there must be grain to store; kin_council: a shared store needs an agreed rule of access.
newNodes.rationale: cereal_cultivation: there must be grain to store; kin_council: a shared store needs an agreed rule of access.
newNodes.desc: The village keeps its grain in common storehouses under agreed rules, so a household with a poor crop can draw on the common stock.
newNodes.effectRationale: A pooled reserve lets households ride out a shortfall without going hungry.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_granaries (A5) is a state buffer stock sold in dearth; this is a village pool held in common.

newNodes.name: Transhumance
newNodes.emerged: ~5,000 BCE seasonal herd movement in the Zagros and the Alps (isotopic evidence)
newNodes.prereqRationale: sheep_goat: herds to move; seasonal_round: the scheduled movement between seasonal places.
newNodes.rationale: sheep_goat: herds to move; seasonal_round: the scheduled movement between seasonal places.
newNodes.desc: Herders move flocks between summer mountain pastures and winter lowlands along customary routes, so neither range is grazed bare.
newNodes.effectRationale: Rotating pastures by season keeps grazing fresh, so herds yield more.
newNodes.distinctFrom: stinted_commons (A6) caps beasts on one common; transhumance moves herds between distant pastures.

newNodes.name: Craft specialization
newNodes.emerged: ~6,000 BCE Halaf workshop pottery; ~4,500 BCE Varna goldsmiths
newNodes.prereqRationale: pottery_open_fired: the first workshop craft; gift_exchange: a demand for crafted valuables beyond the household.
newNodes.rationale: pottery_open_fired: the first workshop craft; gift_exchange: a demand for crafted valuables beyond the household.
newNodes.desc: Some households work part-time as potters, bead-makers or smiths and exchange their wares for food.
newNodes.effectRationale: Exchange for food lets a share of people live by craft, enlarging the specialist class.
newNodes.distinctFrom: craft_guilds (A5) regulates organised trades; this is the first appearance of specialists at all.

newNodes.name: Barter of staples
newNodes.emerged: ~7,000 BCE obsidian, shell and grain exchanged between Anatolian and Levantine villages
newNodes.prereqRationale: gift_exchange: the older exchange network; cereal_cultivation: a storable staple to offer in exchange.
newNodes.rationale: gift_exchange: the older exchange network; cereal_cultivation: a storable staple to offer in exchange.
newNodes.desc: Villagers trade surplus grain, salt and stone with neighbours at agreed equivalents, without waiting for a gift to be returned.
newNodes.effectRationale: Surplus held in store can be traded away at once, so stocks reach those who need them sooner.
newNodes.distinctFrom: gift_exchange is reciprocal and delayed between partners; barter is an immediate exchange of equivalents.

newNodes.name: Reciprocal work parties
newNodes.emerged: ~7,400 BCE Çatalhöyük houses rebuilt in place by neighbouring households (inferred)
newNodes.prereqRationale: communal_feasts: the host feeds the workers; mudbrick: house-raising is the commonest task.
newNodes.rationale: communal_feasts: the host feeds the workers; mudbrick: house-raising is the commonest task.
newNodes.desc: Households call on neighbours to raise houses and bring in harvests, repaying with food, drink and labour in turn.
newNodes.effectRationale: Pooled neighbours raise a house in days, so each dwelling costs less labour.
newNodes.distinctFrom: corvee_labour (A3) is labour owed to a ruler; work parties are reciprocal among equals.

newNodes.name: Ration distribution
newNodes.emerged: ~3,100 BCE Uruk bevelled-rim ration bowls; ~2,100 BCE Ur III ration lists
newNodes.prereqRationale: temple_economy: the institution that feeds its dependants; token_counting: rations are counted and recorded.
newNodes.rationale: temple_economy: the institution that feeds its dependants; token_counting: rations are counted and recorded.
newNodes.desc: Temple and palace issue standard monthly rations of barley, oil and wool to workers, widows and orphans on their lists.
newNodes.effectRationale: Dependants on the ration lists are fed even in bad years, so fewer die of famine.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_granaries (A5) sells and issues stock in dearth; rations are a routine, standing payment in kind.

newNodes.name: Interest-bearing loans
newNodes.emerged: ~2,400 BCE Lagash barley and silver loans at interest; ~1,754 BCE Hammurabi fixes the rates
newNodes.prereqRationale: temple_economy: temples were the first lenders; standard_weights: loans of silver are measured by weight.
newNodes.rationale: temple_economy: temples were the first lenders; standard_weights: loans of silver are measured by weight.
newNodes.desc: Temples and merchants lend barley and silver at fixed interest, recorded on sealed tablets, to finance seed and caravans.
newNodes.effectRationale: Credit finances caravans to distant markets, so merchants act on price differences sooner.
newNodes.distinctFrom: debt_remission cancels debts; this is the credit contract itself.

newNodes.name: Wage and hire tariffs
newNodes.emerged: ~1,800 BCE Laws of Eshnunna fix harvesters' wages and the hire of oxen and boats
newNodes.prereqRationale: law_code: tariffs are clauses of written law; corvee_labour: organised labour gangs precede hired labour.
newNodes.rationale: law_code: tariffs are clauses of written law; corvee_labour: organised labour gangs precede hired labour.
newNodes.desc: The law fixes what a harvester, an ox-team or a boat earns for a day's hire, so workers can be hired without haggling.
newNodes.effectRationale: A known daily wage lets labourers travel to wherever harvest hands are needed.
newNodes.distinctFrom: corvee_labour is unpaid obligation; hire tariffs set the price of free hired work.

newNodes.name: Private banking houses
newNodes.emerged: ~600 BCE Egibi house of Babylon takes deposits and makes loans; ~440 BCE Murashu house finances tenants
newNodes.prereqRationale: interest_bearing_credit: the loan contract; land_registry: registered land serves as security.
newNodes.rationale: interest_bearing_credit: the loan contract; land_registry: registered land serves as security.
newNodes.desc: Family firms take deposits, pay on written orders and lend against land, linking farmers, merchants and the treasury.
newNodes.effectRationale: Advances against harvests let farmers and merchants sell stock without waiting for a buyer to bring silver.
newNodes.distinctFrom: interest_bearing_credit is the single loan; banking houses are standing firms holding deposits.

newNodes.name: Weekly rest day
newNodes.emerged: ~600 BCE Deuteronomic law extends sabbath rest to servants and hired workers
newNodes.prereqRationale: scriptural_canon: the rest day is a written religious command; hire_tariffs: it protects hired workers.
newNodes.rationale: scriptural_canon: the rest day is a written religious command; hire_tariffs: it protects hired workers.
newNodes.desc: One day in seven, servants, hired workers and draught animals are released from work by law.
newNodes.effectRationale: A guaranteed rest day removes a constant source of resentment among labourers.
newNodes.distinctFrom: Working-hours limits in factory_inspection (A8) are enforced by inspectors; this is a customary rest day.

newNodes.name: Water-turn shares
newNodes.emerged: ~500 BCE Achaemenid kings grant qanat water to its builders for five generations (Polybius)
newNodes.prereqRationale: qanat: the channel whose flow is shared; water_rights: the legal frame for shares.
newNodes.rationale: qanat: the channel whose flow is shared; water_rights: the legal frame for shares.
newNodes.desc: Those who dig a channel own its flow in timed turns that can be inherited or sold, so new channels are dug.
newNodes.effectRationale: Secure, tradable water shares reward new channels, so more land is watered and yields rise.
newNodes.distinctFrom: water_rights fixes duties on existing canals; water-turn shares make new water a tradable property.

newNodes.name: Sea loans
newNodes.emerged: ~400 BCE Athenian bottomry loans repayable only if the ship returns
newNodes.prereqRationale: banking_houses: lenders with capital; trade: seaborne trade to finance.
newNodes.rationale: banking_houses: lenders with capital; trade: seaborne trade to finance.
newNodes.desc: Lenders advance money on a ship and cargo, repayable only if the voyage succeeds, so the merchant does not bear the risk of loss alone.
newNodes.effectRationale: Shifting shipwreck risk to lenders lowers what merchants must charge for carrying bulk goods.
newNodes.distinctFrom: insurance_underwriting (A7) prices risk separately from credit; the sea loan combines loan and insurance.

newNodes.name: Public physicians
newNodes.emerged: ~525 BCE Democedes paid as public physician by Aegina and Athens (Herodotus)
newNodes.prereqRationale: medicine_hippocratic: a trained profession to hire; citizen_assembly: the city votes the salary.
newNodes.rationale: medicine_hippocratic: a trained profession to hire; citizen_assembly: the city votes the salary.
newNodes.desc: The city pays a salaried physician to treat its citizens, rich and poor alike.
newNodes.effectRationale: Treatment available to all citizens reduces deaths from injury and illness.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_health_board (A7) holds powers of quarantine; public physicians treat individual patients.

newNodes.name: Water commissioners
newNodes.emerged: ~11 BCE Roman cura aquarum; ~97 CE Frontinus' De aquaeductu
newNodes.prereqRationale: aqueduct_arcade: the supply to administer; appointed_officials: a permanent office with staff.
newNodes.rationale: aqueduct_arcade: the supply to administer; appointed_officials: a permanent office with staff.
newNodes.desc: A permanent office maintains the aqueducts, licenses private connections and punishes theft of water.
newNodes.effectRationale: Reliable public water lets crowded blocks stay habitable, so more people live in each dwelling.
newNodes.distinctFrom: building_regulation governs construction; the water commission runs a public supply.

newNodes.name: Child-support foundations
newNodes.emerged: ~97 CE Nerva's and Trajan's alimenta for freeborn children in Italian towns
newNodes.prereqRationale: public_granaries: the state already feeds citizens; municipal_charter: towns administer the funds.
newNodes.rationale: public_granaries: the state already feeds citizens; municipal_charter: towns administer the funds.
newNodes.desc: Endowed funds pay a monthly allowance to poor children in each town, financed by interest on loans to local landowners.
newNodes.effectRationale: A guaranteed allowance for children protects them first when food is scarce.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_granaries feeds citizens at large; alimenta is targeted at children.

newNodes.name: Commenda partnership
newNodes.emerged: ~800 CE Islamic qirad contracts; ~1,072 CE Venetian colleganza
newNodes.prereqRationale: commercial_law: the partnership is enforced by merchant courts.
newNodes.rationale: commercial_law: the partnership is enforced by merchant courts.
newNodes.desc: A stay-at-home investor funds a travelling merchant for one voyage and they split the profit, so a young trader without capital can start out.
newNodes.effectRationale: Partnerships give poor but able traders capital, so they rise into the merchant class faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: joint_stock pools many investors in a permanent company; the commenda is a two-party contract for one venture.

newNodes.name: Hospitals
newNodes.emerged: ~805 CE Baghdad bimaristan; ~1,136 CE Pantokrator hospital, Constantinople
newNodes.prereqRationale: pharmacology: physicians with a pharmacopoeia staff the wards; state_religion: hospitals were founded as pious endowments.
newNodes.rationale: pharmacology: physicians with a pharmacopoeia staff the wards; state_religion: hospitals were founded as pious endowments.
newNodes.desc: Endowed hospitals with wards, physicians and pharmacies take in the sick without charge.
newNodes.effectRationale: Nursing and treatment in wards cut deaths from illness among the poor.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_physicians (A5) are salaried doctors; hospitals are permanent institutions with beds.

newNodes.name: Stinted commons
newNodes.emerged: ~1,240 CE English manor-court by-laws limit beasts per holding on the common
newNodes.prereqRationale: manorialism: the manor court that makes and enforces the by-laws.
newNodes.rationale: manorialism: the manor court that makes and enforces the by-laws.
newNodes.desc: The village court limits how many beasts each holding may graze on the common, so the pasture is not overgrazed.
newNodes.effectRationale: A capped common keeps its grass, so herds on it yield more.
newNodes.distinctFrom: forest_law reserves woods for a lord; stinting shares a pasture among commoners.

newNodes.name: Mutual-aid fraternities
newNodes.emerged: ~1,200 CE guild and parish fraternities fund sick members and burials
newNodes.prereqRationale: craft_guilds: fraternities grew from guild membership; municipal_charter: they were chartered urban bodies.
newNodes.rationale: craft_guilds: fraternities grew from guild membership; municipal_charter: they were chartered urban bodies.
newNodes.desc: Members pay regular dues into a common box that supports them when sick and pays for their burial.
newNodes.effectRationale: A sickness fund keeps a household fed while its earner cannot work.
newNodes.distinctFrom: craft_guilds regulates a trade; fraternities insure their members.

newNodes.name: Apprenticeship indentures
newNodes.emerged: ~1,268 CE Paris Livre des métiers fixes apprenticeship terms
newNodes.prereqRationale: craft_guilds: guilds register and supervise the indentures.
newNodes.rationale: craft_guilds: guilds register and supervise the indentures.
newNodes.desc: A written indenture binds a youth to a master for years of training in return for board and the right to become a journeyman.
newNodes.effectRationale: Formal training produces more skilled craftsmen, so the specialist class can be larger.
newNodes.distinctFrom: craft_guilds governs masters; apprenticeship is the training contract that makes them.

newNodes.name: Water boards
newNodes.emerged: ~1,255 CE Hoogheemraadschap van Rijnland: landholders govern dikes and drainage
newNodes.prereqRationale: water_rights: the duty to maintain banks; municipal_charter: a chartered self-governing body with its own levy.
newNodes.rationale: water_rights: the duty to maintain banks; municipal_charter: a chartered self-governing body with its own levy.
newNodes.desc: Landholders elect a board that levies a rate, keeps the dikes and drains the polders.
newNodes.effectRationale: Maintained dikes stop floods ruining harvests, and drained land is more fertile.
newNodes.distinctFrom: water_rights allocates water; water boards are standing bodies that build and keep flood defences.

newNodes.name: Insurance underwriting
newNodes.emerged: ~1,688 CE Lloyd's coffee-house underwriters; ~1,693 CE Halley's life table
newNodes.prereqRationale: probability_statistics: premiums are priced from loss rates; stock_exchange: an organised market of risk-takers.
newNodes.rationale: probability_statistics: premiums are priced from loss rates; stock_exchange: an organised market of risk-takers.
newNodes.desc: Underwriters take a share of a ship's or a life's risk for a premium priced on recorded losses.
newNodes.effectRationale: Cheap, priced insurance lowers the risk charge on every bulk cargo.
newNodes.distinctFrom: maritime_loans fold insurance into credit; underwriting sells risk cover on its own.

newNodes.name: Organised fire-fighting
newNodes.emerged: ~1,672 CE Amsterdam fire-hose brigades; ~1,680 CE London Fire Office
newNodes.prereqRationale: building_regulation: fire prevention by law comes first; municipal_charter: towns fund and command the brigades.
newNodes.rationale: building_regulation: fire prevention by law comes first; municipal_charter: towns fund and command the brigades.
newNodes.desc: Towns keep engines, hoses and trained crews ready to answer any fire.
newNodes.effectRationale: Fires are put out before they spread, so houses last longer.
newNodes.distinctFrom: building_regulation prevents fires by design; brigades fight them when they start.

newNodes.name: Turnpike trusts
newNodes.emerged: ~1,663 CE first English turnpike act; ~1,706 CE turnpike trusts
newNodes.prereqRationale: customs_tolls: the toll as a source of finance; road_paved: the engineered road it pays for.
newNodes.rationale: customs_tolls: the toll as a source of finance; road_paved: the engineered road it pays for.
newNodes.desc: Trusts collect tolls from road users and spend them on resurfacing and straightening the highway.
newNodes.effectRationale: Tolls pay for maintained surfaces, so coaches and wagons travel faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: customs_tolls raises revenue; turnpike trusts spend road tolls on the road itself.

newNodes.name: Friendly societies
newNodes.emerged: ~1,793 CE Rose's Act registers friendly societies
newNodes.prereqRationale: mutual_aid_fraternities: the older mutual fund; coined_wage: weekly dues paid from money wages.
newNodes.rationale: mutual_aid_fraternities: the older mutual fund; coined_wage: weekly dues paid from money wages.
newNodes.desc: Wage-earners pay weekly into registered societies that pay benefit in sickness, old age and death.
newNodes.effectRationale: Sick pay and burial money keep wage-earning families from destitution in hard years.
newNodes.distinctFrom: mutual_aid_fraternities are guild bodies; friendly societies are open, registered insurance clubs.

newNodes.name: Social insurance
newNodes.emerged: ~1,883 CE German sickness insurance; ~1,889 CE old-age and invalidity insurance
newNodes.prereqRationale: friendly_societies: the voluntary model made compulsory; official_statistics: contributions are set from statistics of sickness and age.
newNodes.rationale: friendly_societies: the voluntary model made compulsory; official_statistics: contributions are set from statistics of sickness and age.
newNodes.desc: The law requires workers and employers to pay into funds that cover sickness, accident and old age.
newNodes.effectRationale: Compulsory sickness cover brings treatment to every insured worker, and security in old age removes a major grievance.
newNodes.distinctFrom: friendly_societies is voluntary; social insurance is compulsory and state-backed.

newNodes.name: Municipal waterworks
newNodes.emerged: ~1,842 CE Croton Aqueduct, New York; ~1,859 CE London main drainage
newNodes.prereqRationale: sanitary_engineering: filtered water and sewers as technique; public_health_board: the authority that commissions them.
newNodes.rationale: sanitary_engineering: filtered water and sewers as technique; public_health_board: the authority that commissions them.
newNodes.desc: The city builds and runs its own filtered water supply and sewers for every street.
newNodes.effectRationale: Clean water and sewers end cholera and typhoid outbreaks, cutting deaths at every age.
newNodes.distinctFrom: sanitary_engineering is the technique; this is the civic duty to supply every street.

newNodes.name: Compulsory vaccination
newNodes.emerged: ~1,807 CE Bavarian vaccination mandate; ~1,853 CE UK Vaccination Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: vaccination: the procedure; public_health_board: the authority that enforces it.
newNodes.rationale: vaccination: the procedure; public_health_board: the authority that enforces it.
newNodes.desc: The law requires every infant to be vaccinated against smallpox and records each vaccination.
newNodes.effectRationale: Universal vaccination ends smallpox epidemics, a landmark fall in deaths.
newNodes.distinctFrom: vaccination is the medical technique; this is the legal duty that makes coverage universal.

newNodes.name: Labour exchanges
newNodes.emerged: ~1,894 CE German municipal labour exchanges; ~1,909 CE UK Labour Exchanges Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: merit_civil_service: public offices run by trained clerks; telegraph: vacancies are posted between towns.
newNodes.rationale: merit_civil_service: public offices run by trained clerks; telegraph: vacancies are posted between towns.
newNodes.desc: Public offices list vacancies and job-seekers and match them across the country.
newNodes.effectRationale: Known vacancies in distant towns draw job-seekers further than rumour would.
newNodes.distinctFrom: hire_tariffs set wages; labour exchanges match workers to jobs.

newNodes.name: Workmen's compensation
newNodes.emerged: ~1,884 CE German accident insurance; ~1,897 CE UK Workmen's Compensation Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: factory_inspection: the state already polices workplace hazards; labour_unions: unions pressed the claim.
newNodes.rationale: factory_inspection: the state already polices workplace hazards; labour_unions: unions pressed the claim.
newNodes.desc: Employers must compensate workers injured on the job, whoever was at fault.
newNodes.effectRationale: An injured worker's family keeps an income, so it does not starve in a hard year.
newNodes.distinctFrom: factory_inspection prevents accidents; compensation pays for them.

newNodes.name: Industrial arbitration
newNodes.emerged: ~1,894 CE New Zealand Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Act; ~1,896 CE UK Conciliation Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: labour_unions: organised parties to a dispute; civil_code OR common_law: a court tradition to host the tribunal, in either legal family.
newNodes.rationale: labour_unions: organised parties to a dispute; civil_code OR common_law: a court tradition to host the tribunal, in either legal family.
newNodes.desc: Disputes between unions and employers go to a conciliation board or arbitration court instead of a strike.
newNodes.effectRationale: Settling disputes by award instead of strikes and lockouts costs far less lost output.
newNodes.distinctFrom: labour_unions organises workers; arbitration settles their disputes without a stoppage.

newNodes.name: Minimum wage
newNodes.emerged: ~1,896 CE Victoria wages boards; ~1,909 CE UK Trade Boards Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: labour_unions: organised pressure for a floor; factory_inspection: inspectors who can enforce it.
newNodes.rationale: labour_unions: organised pressure for a floor; factory_inspection: inspectors who can enforce it.
newNodes.desc: Wage boards set a legal floor under the pay of the lowest-paid trades.
newNodes.effectRationale: A wage floor leaves poor households a margin to absorb dearer food.
newNodes.distinctFrom: hire_tariffs fixes customary rates; the minimum wage is a floor, not a fixed price.

newNodes.name: Commodity exchange
newNodes.emerged: ~1,848 CE Chicago Board of Trade; ~1,865 CE standardised grain futures
newNodes.prereqRationale: stock_exchange: the organised exchange model; telegraph: prices quoted between markets in minutes.
newNodes.rationale: stock_exchange: the organised exchange model; telegraph: prices quoted between markets in minutes.
newNodes.desc: Graded grain and cotton are traded for present and future delivery on a regulated exchange.
newNodes.effectRationale: Grading and futures let elevators sell stored grain the moment a price is offered.
newNodes.distinctFrom: market_fairs meet periodically for goods in hand; the exchange trades graded lots continuously and forward.

newNodes.name: Housing reform acts
newNodes.emerged: ~1,875 CE Artisans' Dwellings Act; ~1,890 CE Housing of the Working Classes Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: building_regulation: standards to apply; public_health_board: slums condemned as a health danger.
newNodes.rationale: building_regulation: standards to apply; public_health_board: slums condemned as a health danger.
newNodes.desc: Councils may condemn unfit slums and require new dwellings to meet standards of light, drainage and soundness.
newNodes.effectRationale: Sound construction standards mean dwellings last longer.
newNodes.distinctFrom: building_regulation governs height and fire; housing acts set minimum standards of habitability.

newNodes.name: Deposit insurance
newNodes.emerged: ~1,933 CE US Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
newNodes.prereqRationale: central_banking: a lender behind the banks; limited_liability: bank shareholders' liability is limited, so depositors need cover.
newNodes.rationale: central_banking: a lender behind the banks; limited_liability: bank shareholders' liability is limited, so depositors need cover.
newNodes.desc: A public fund guarantees ordinary deposits, so savers no longer lose everything when a bank fails.
newNodes.effectRationale: Household savings survive bank failures, so families can draw on them in a shortfall.
newNodes.distinctFrom: central_banking manages the currency; deposit insurance protects the individual saver.

newNodes.name: Countercyclical demand management
newNodes.emerged: ~1,936 CE Keynes' General Theory; ~1,946 CE US Employment Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: central_banking: monetary levers; income_tax: fiscal levers; official_statistics: national accounts to steer by.
newNodes.rationale: central_banking: monetary levers; income_tax: fiscal levers; official_statistics: national accounts to steer by.
newNodes.desc: The state cuts taxes and spends in slumps, and restrains demand in booms, to keep output steady.
newNodes.effectRationale: Shallower slumps mean unrest and lost work cost less output.
newNodes.distinctFrom: central_planning sets output by plan; demand management steers a market economy.

newNodes.name: Managed exchange rates
newNodes.emerged: ~1,944 CE Bretton Woods agreement; ~1,945 CE International Monetary Fund
newNodes.prereqRationale: central_banking: banks that hold reserves and defend a parity; international_organizations: the fund that coordinates them.
newNodes.rationale: central_banking: banks that hold reserves and defend a parity; international_organizations: the fund that coordinates them.
newNodes.desc: Currencies are pegged to an agreed standard and defended by central banks with a shared reserve fund.
newNodes.effectRationale: Stable exchange rates remove currency risk from every shipment.
newNodes.distinctFrom: multilateral_trade_rules binds tariffs; this binds the currencies trade is paid in.

newNodes.name: Farm price support
newNodes.emerged: ~1,933 CE US Agricultural Adjustment Act and Commodity Credit Corporation; ~1,962 CE EEC Common Agricultural Policy
newNodes.prereqRationale: public_granaries: state stockholding; commodity_exchange: a market price for the state to support.
newNodes.rationale: public_granaries: state stockholding; commodity_exchange: a market price for the state to support.
newNodes.desc: The state buys surplus grain at a guaranteed price and holds it in reserve stocks.
newNodes.effectRationale: Support buying builds large public reserves, so stores can hold more years of demand.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_granaries is a city's famine stock; price support is a national reserve bought to hold up farm prices.

newNodes.name: Microfinance
newNodes.emerged: ~1,983 CE Grameen Bank, Bangladesh
newNodes.prereqRationale: cooperatives: group lending and joint liability; central_banking: a regulated banking system to charter it.
newNodes.rationale: cooperatives: group lending and joint liability; central_banking: a regulated banking system to charter it.
newNodes.desc: Small loans are made to groups of poor borrowers who guarantee each other, without collateral.
newNodes.effectRationale: Capital for the poorest lets them start trades, so they rise out of labouring poverty faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: cooperatives share a business; microfinance lends to individuals backed by group guarantee.

newNodes.name: Special economic zones
newNodes.emerged: ~1,959 CE Shannon Free Zone, Ireland; ~1,980 CE Shenzhen
newNodes.prereqRationale: multilateral_trade_rules: export zones were designed to plug into the GATT trading order.
newNodes.rationale: multilateral_trade_rules: export zones were designed to plug into the GATT trading order.
newNodes.desc: Designated districts offer foreign firms low tariffs, light regulation and ready sites, drawing industry and workers.
newNodes.effectRationale: Factory jobs in the zones draw migrants from the countryside.
newNodes.distinctFrom: customs_union removes tariffs between states; a zone removes them for one district.

newNodes.name: Collective bargaining law
newNodes.emerged: ~1,935 CE US National Labor Relations Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: labour_unions: the bargaining party; industrial_arbitration: the state's earlier role in labour disputes.
newNodes.rationale: labour_unions: the bargaining party; industrial_arbitration: the state's earlier role in labour disputes.
newNodes.desc: Employers must recognise a union chosen by their workers and bargain with it in good faith.
newNodes.effectRationale: Recognised bargaining turns workplace complaints into contracts, so grievance builds more slowly.
newNodes.distinctFrom: labour_unions makes combination legal; this law obliges employers to bargain.

newNodes.name: Unemployment insurance
newNodes.emerged: ~1,911 CE UK National Insurance Act, Part II; ~1,935 CE US Social Security Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: social_insurance: the contributory model; labour_exchanges: benefit is paid while the claimant seeks work through the exchange.
newNodes.rationale: social_insurance: the contributory model; labour_exchanges: benefit is paid while the claimant seeks work through the exchange.
newNodes.desc: Insured workers who lose their jobs draw a weekly benefit while they look for work.
newNodes.effectRationale: Laid-off workers keep an income, so slumps cause less disorder and lost output.
newNodes.distinctFrom: social_insurance covers sickness and age; this covers loss of work.

newNodes.name: Occupational safety agencies
newNodes.emerged: ~1,970 CE US Occupational Safety and Health Act; ~1,974 CE UK Health and Safety at Work Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: factory_inspection: the inspectorate; workmens_compensation: employers already bear the cost of injury.
newNodes.rationale: factory_inspection: the inspectorate; workmens_compensation: employers already bear the cost of injury.
newNodes.desc: An agency sets exposure limits and safety standards for every workplace, not only factories.
newNodes.effectRationale: Standards for chemicals, machinery and construction cut deaths at work.
newNodes.distinctFrom: factory_inspection covers mills and hours; this sets scientific exposure limits across all work.

newNodes.name: Public vocational training
newNodes.emerged: ~1,917 CE US Smith–Hughes Act; ~1,969 CE German Vocational Training Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: apprenticeship: the training contract; compulsory_education: the school system it is joined to.
newNodes.rationale: apprenticeship: the training contract; compulsory_education: the school system it is joined to.
newNodes.desc: Schools and employers jointly train young people in trades to a national standard.
newNodes.effectRationale: Recognised qualifications let workers' children move into skilled trades faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: apprenticeship is a private contract with a master; this is a public, certified system.

newNodes.name: Equal pay law
newNodes.emerged: ~1,951 CE ILO Equal Remuneration Convention; ~1,963 CE US Equal Pay Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: minimum_wage: the state already regulates pay; womens_suffrage: women voters pressed for the law.
newNodes.rationale: minimum_wage: the state already regulates pay; womens_suffrage: women voters pressed for the law.
newNodes.desc: Employers must pay women the same as men for the same work.
newNodes.effectRationale: Women can enter skilled and professional work on equal terms, so the specialist classes can be larger.
newNodes.distinctFrom: civil_rights_law bans discrimination broadly; equal pay governs wages for the same work.

newNodes.name: Guest-worker programmes
newNodes.emerged: ~1,942 CE Bracero Program; ~1,961 CE German–Turkish recruitment agreement
newNodes.prereqRationale: labour_exchanges: recruitment offices; sworn_treaties: bilateral recruitment agreements.
newNodes.rationale: labour_exchanges: recruitment offices; sworn_treaties: bilateral recruitment agreements.
newNodes.desc: States agree to recruit workers abroad on fixed contracts to fill labour shortages.
newNodes.effectRationale: Organised recruitment moves workers across borders in large numbers.
newNodes.distinctFrom: refugee_protection admits those fleeing danger; guest-worker schemes recruit labour by contract.

newNodes.name: Universal social security
newNodes.emerged: ~1,942 CE Beveridge Report; ~1,948 CE UK National Insurance and National Assistance Acts
newNodes.prereqRationale: social_insurance: the contributory schemes unified; income_tax: general taxation funds the safety net.
newNodes.rationale: social_insurance: the contributory schemes unified; income_tax: general taxation funds the safety net.
newNodes.desc: Every citizen is covered from cradle to grave: insurance for all and a national safety net beneath it.
newNodes.effectRationale: A universal safety net means no one starves in a crisis and households weather shortfalls.
newNodes.distinctFrom: social_insurance covers insured workers; universal social security covers every citizen.

newNodes.name: School meals
newNodes.emerged: ~1,906 CE UK Education (Provision of Meals) Act; ~1,946 CE US National School Lunch Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: compulsory_education: children are in school to be fed; poor_law: public relief in kind.
newNodes.rationale: compulsory_education: children are in school to be fed; poor_law: public relief in kind.
newNodes.desc: Schools serve every pupil a free or cheap midday meal.
newNodes.effectRationale: A daily meal at school protects children when food is scarce at home.
newNodes.distinctFrom: alimenta pays a cash allowance; school meals feed children directly.

newNodes.name: Conditional cash transfers
newNodes.emerged: ~1,997 CE Mexico Progresa; ~2,003 CE Brazil Bolsa Família
newNodes.prereqRationale: school_meals: welfare tied to school attendance; official_statistics: a registry to target poor households.
newNodes.rationale: school_meals: welfare tied to school attendance; official_statistics: a registry to target poor households.
newNodes.desc: Poor mothers receive monthly cash on condition that children attend school and health checks.
newNodes.effectRationale: Paid attendance keeps poor children in school, and the cash protects them in dearth.
newNodes.distinctFrom: school_meals feeds pupils; transfers pay families for schooling and health visits.

newNodes.name: Refugee protection
newNodes.emerged: ~1,951 CE Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees
newNodes.prereqRationale: human_rights: the right to asylum; international_organizations: the agency that registers refugees.
newNodes.rationale: human_rights: the right to asylum; international_organizations: the agency that registers refugees.
newNodes.desc: States may not send refugees back to danger and grant them legal status and relief.
newNodes.effectRationale: Assured asylum lets people fleeing war travel further to safety.
newNodes.distinctFrom: guest_worker_programmes recruit labour; refugee protection admits people fleeing danger.

newNodes.name: Universal health care
newNodes.emerged: ~1,948 CE UK National Health Service
newNodes.prereqRationale: social_insurance: health cover by contribution; public_hospitals: the hospital network nationalised or contracted.
newNodes.rationale: social_insurance: health cover by contribution; public_hospitals: the hospital network nationalised or contracted.
newNodes.desc: Medical care is free at the point of use for every resident, paid for from taxes or universal insurance.
newNodes.effectRationale: Everyone can see a doctor and enter hospital, a landmark fall in deaths.
newNodes.distinctFrom: social_insurance covers insured workers; universal care covers every resident.

newNodes.name: Mass immunization programmes
newNodes.emerged: ~1,955 CE US polio vaccination campaign; ~1,974 CE WHO Expanded Programme on Immunization
newNodes.prereqRationale: compulsory_vaccination: the duty to vaccinate; vaccine_lab: new vaccines for measles, polio and diphtheria.
newNodes.rationale: compulsory_vaccination: the duty to vaccinate; vaccine_lab: new vaccines for measles, polio and diphtheria.
newNodes.desc: Health services vaccinate every child against measles, polio, diphtheria and whooping cough on a fixed schedule.
newNodes.effectRationale: Measles and whooping cough kill malnourished children first; immunised children survive famine years.
newNodes.distinctFrom: compulsory_vaccination covers smallpox; this schedules many vaccines for every child.

newNodes.name: International health regulations
newNodes.emerged: ~1,948 CE World Health Organization; ~1,951 CE International Sanitary Regulations
newNodes.prereqRationale: public_health_board: national quarantine powers; international_organizations: the body that harmonises them.
newNodes.rationale: public_health_board: national quarantine powers; international_organizations: the body that harmonises them.
newNodes.desc: States report outbreaks to a common body and apply agreed, limited quarantine rules at ports and borders.
newNodes.effectRationale: Agreed rules replace arbitrary quarantines that held up cargo, and early warning contains epidemics.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_health_board acts within one polity; these rules coordinate between polities.

newNodes.name: Drug regulation
newNodes.emerged: ~1,938 CE US Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act; ~1,962 CE Kefauver–Harris amendments
newNodes.prereqRationale: public_health_board: a regulating authority; sulfonamides: the 1937 sulfanilamide poisoning prompted the 1938 Act.
newNodes.rationale: public_health_board: a regulating authority; sulfonamides: the 1937 sulfanilamide poisoning prompted the 1938 Act.
newNodes.desc: New medicines must be proven safe and effective in trials before sale.
newNodes.effectRationale: Only tested drugs reach patients, so university medicine saves more lives.
newNodes.distinctFrom: pharmacology compiles remedies; regulation requires proof before sale.

newNodes.name: Primary health care
newNodes.emerged: ~1,968 CE Chinese barefoot doctors; ~1,978 CE Alma-Ata Declaration
newNodes.prereqRationale: public_physicians: publicly paid first-line care; international_health_regulations: the WHO framework that set the Alma-Ata goals.
newNodes.rationale: public_physicians: publicly paid first-line care; international_health_regulations: the WHO framework that set the Alma-Ata goals.
newNodes.desc: Trained village health workers give basic care, clean water advice and maternal care in every community.
newNodes.effectRationale: Care reaches villages without hospitals, cutting deaths from common illness and in famine.
newNodes.distinctFrom: national_health_service is a hospital-based system; primary care puts trained workers in every village.

newNodes.name: Public housing
newNodes.emerged: ~1,919 CE UK Addison Act; ~1,923 CE Vienna municipal housing programme
newNodes.prereqRationale: housing_acts: standards and slum clearance; income_tax: subsidy from general taxation.
newNodes.rationale: housing_acts: standards and slum clearance; income_tax: subsidy from general taxation.
newNodes.desc: Councils build and let standard homes at controlled rents on a large scale.
newNodes.effectRationale: Standard designs built in long runs take less labour per home.
newNodes.distinctFrom: housing_acts set standards; public housing builds the homes.

newNodes.name: National highway programmes
newNodes.emerged: ~1,934 CE Reichsautobahn programme; ~1,956 CE US Interstate Highway Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: motor_road: the engineered motorway; turnpike_trusts: the older idea of a road financed for through traffic.
newNodes.rationale: motor_road: the engineered motorway; turnpike_trusts: the older idea of a road financed for through traffic.
newNodes.desc: A national authority plans and finances a network of motorways linking every region.
newNodes.effectRationale: A national network lets roads run much further between cities.
newNodes.distinctFrom: turnpike_trusts maintain local roads; a national programme builds a planned trunk network.

newNodes.name: Metropolitan transit authorities
newNodes.emerged: ~1,933 CE London Passenger Transport Board
newNodes.prereqRationale: electric_traction: trams and metros to operate; zoning: planned residential districts for transit to serve.
newNodes.rationale: electric_traction: trams and metros to operate; zoning: planned residential districts for transit to serve.
newNodes.desc: One public authority runs a city's buses, trams and metro as a single network.
newNodes.effectRationale: Integrated transit lets workers commute from further out, widening the city's hinterland.
newNodes.distinctFrom: zoning governs land use; the transit authority moves people between zones.

newNodes.name: Planned new towns
newNodes.emerged: ~1,903 CE Letchworth garden city; ~1,946 CE UK New Towns Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: housing_acts: overcrowding to relieve; railway: a line to link the new town to the old.
newNodes.rationale: housing_acts: overcrowding to relieve; railway: a line to link the new town to the old.
newNodes.desc: Development corporations build complete new towns, with homes, factories and services, to take people from crowded cities.
newNodes.effectRationale: Planned overspill moves large parties of settlers at once.
newNodes.distinctFrom: planned_cities lays out one town; new towns are a programme of founding.

newNodes.name: River basin authorities
newNodes.emerged: ~1,933 CE Tennessee Valley Authority
newNodes.prereqRationale: water_boards: a body that governs water by catchment; hydroelectric: dams that pay for the scheme.
newNodes.rationale: water_boards: a body that governs water by catchment; hydroelectric: dams that pay for the scheme.
newNodes.desc: One authority manages a whole river basin's dams, locks, flood control and power.
newNodes.effectRationale: Locked, regulated rivers carry barges cheaply, and controlled floods spare the fields.
newNodes.distinctFrom: water_boards keep local dikes; a basin authority plans an entire river.

newNodes.name: Soil conservation
newNodes.emerged: ~1,935 CE US Soil Conservation Service
newNodes.prereqRationale: nature_conservation: protection of land as a public duty; agricultural_chemistry: soil science to diagnose erosion.
newNodes.rationale: nature_conservation: protection of land as a public duty; agricultural_chemistry: soil science to diagnose erosion.
newNodes.desc: Advisers and grants teach contour ploughing, terracing and shelter belts to stop soil blowing and washing away.
newNodes.effectRationale: Soil kept on the fields keeps its fertility, so land yields more.
newNodes.distinctFrom: nature_conservation sets land aside; soil conservation keeps farmland productive.

newNodes.name: Fisheries management
newNodes.emerged: ~1,976 CE US Magnuson Fishery Act; ~1,982 CE UN Law of the Sea exclusive economic zones
newNodes.prereqRationale: nature_conservation: protection of living resources; law_of_nations: maritime jurisdiction over coastal waters.
newNodes.rationale: nature_conservation: protection of living resources; law_of_nations: maritime jurisdiction over coastal waters.
newNodes.desc: Coastal states set catch quotas in their waters to let fish stocks recover.
newNodes.effectRationale: Recovered stocks give larger sustainable catches.
newNodes.distinctFrom: stinted_commons caps grazing on land; this caps catches at sea.

newNodes.name: Public works relief
newNodes.emerged: ~1,933 CE US Public Works Administration and Civilian Conservation Corps; ~1,935 CE Works Progress Administration
newNodes.prereqRationale: poor_law: public relief of the able-bodied; income_tax: the revenue that pays relief wages.
newNodes.rationale: poor_law: public relief of the able-bodied; income_tax: the revenue that pays relief wages.
newNodes.desc: The state hires the unemployed to build roads, bridges, dams and parks.
newNodes.effectRationale: Organised relief gangs build more road per worker.
newNodes.distinctFrom: corvee_labour is compulsory; relief work is paid work offered to the unemployed.

newLanes.name: Labour
newLanes.scope: Terms of work: hire and wage rules, training contracts, working conditions, workplace safety and compensation, collective bargaining, labour markets and labour migration. Split from society-welfare.

newLanes.name: Public health
newLanes.scope: Collective protection of health: public physicians, hospitals, vaccination duties, drug regulation, primary care and international disease control. Water and sewer works stay in environment-urban (public works).

findings: Dependency changes proposed: 1. manorialism: service_tenure AND heavy_plough becomes service_tenure AND (heavy_plough OR legal_code_roman). The bound-tenant estate (Roman colonate 332 CE, Byzantine and Iberian estates) ploughed with the ard; the heavy plough is one route, not a must-hold. Every other edge in the group was assessed and kept.

abolition (A8) rests on a single A4 atom (legal_code_roman). The natural second atom is social_contract (natural-rights doctrine, 1651), but the node's emerged text opens with Solon (594 BCE), so the chronology rule forbids it. Recommend narrowing emerged to the 1794/1833/1861 acts (Solon as a precursor note) and then adding social_contract.

Leaves bridged by new nodes rather than new edges: central_banking (deposit_insurance, demand_management, managed_exchange_rates, microfinance), stock_exchange (insurance_underwriting, commodity_exchange), poor_law (school_meals, public_works_relief), water_rights (water_turn_shares, water_boards), factory_inspection (workmens_compensation, minimum_wage, occupational_safety), public_granaries (alimenta, price_support), gift_exchange (craft_specialists, barter_exchange), zoning (transit_authority), cooperatives (microfinance). Deliberate leaves: debt_remission, legal_estates, market_fairs, mercantilism, antitrust, abolition, civil_rights_law, climate_accords.

Two lanes declared (labour, public-health), both split from society-welfare. On import, labour_unions and factory_inspection fit the labour lane and public_health_board the public-health lane; they are left in society-welfare here because lane moves are not an audit action.

Thematic gap closed: before this tranche the group had no labour or public-health node before A7 and no welfare node between A3 and A5. New early nodes (food_sharing_norms, communal_storage, ration_distribution, hire_tariffs, public_physicians, alimenta, public_hospitals) give every Age a welfare or labour step.

No treasury: every welfare node acts on mortality, famine deaths, child protection, shortfall absorption, grievance, unrest drag or mobility, never on money. Banking and credit nodes act on trade and price operands.

Pacing: A9 carries 29 new nodes (quota) against 7 existing; per the pacing rule the A9 civics scale must fall accordingly. Several A8/A9 nodes have earliest dates just before their Age window (minimum_wage 1896, unemployment_insurance 1911, school_meals 1906, new_towns 1903); they are placed by when the institution spread.
Operand pressure: demographics.mortalityPerYear is used by 12 nodes in this group (sum 0.39 of cap 0.7); combined with other groups' use it may approach the cap, which the integrator should check.

Comparators: Civ VI base data has no labour, public-health or welfare civics at all (its welfare content is in Gathering Storm or policy cards outside the data file); Civ VII touches them only as policies (Annona, Welfare State, New Deal, Public Works). Most new nodes are therefore none-by-design.
